transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-04
Start: 10:00 AM PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Jensen, Priya Nair (Redwood); Mark Ruiz, Lina Gomez, Evan Park (Embera)

Auto-summary (fireflies): Weekly POC check-in focused on KV/prefix cache hit-rate. Discussion includes wrong-turns in prompt normalization, suggestion to try session affinity, and an action to run a 24h throughput replay.

[00:00] Alex Jensen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Mark Ruiz: Mark here, sorry running a bit late, audio's good.
[00:11] Lina Gomez: Lina, ML. All good.
[00:13] Evan Park: Evan, SRE. I'm on.
[00:15] Alex Jensen: Great. Priya from the Redwood infra team is with me. We pushed two small tuning commits last Friday, one around prefix normalization and one for prefetch window sizing, and want to walk through the hit-rate deltas.
[00:28] Priya Nair: Hi all, quick note — the measurement windows we used are session-level and prefix-level. Session hit-rate jumped from about 24% to 39% after the initial fix, prefix hit-rate up from 11% to 27% on the sample traffic. These are median numbers from the 6h run.
[00:48] Mark Ruiz: Okay that sounds prom— promising, but our catalyzing traffic has lots of short sessions and long chats mixed. Did you stratify by session length?
[00:57] Priya Nair: Yes — we split at 6-turn boundary; long sessions (>=6 turns) saw a higher absolute gain because more prefix reuse opportunities. Short sessions had modest improvements. We noted our prefix normalization merged minor whitespace and punctuation variants, which increased reuse.
[01:18] Lina Gomez: Quick question — how are you normalizing prompts? We had been doing back-end dedupe that was pretty aggressive and maybe losing intent markers.
[01:26] Priya Nair: Good question. Our approach is conservative: normalize whitespace, collapse repeated punctuation, canonicalize common stop tokens, but we keep brackets and special function tokens intact. We avoid stemming or semantic paraphrase — that loses signals.
[01:43] Evan Park: On infra — we saw some transient evictions during the 3am peak in your last run, eviction rate spiked. Is that TTL-based?
[01:51] Alex Jensen: The default eviction policy we used in that run was LRU with a short TTL for prefix entries to avoid stale content. Our thought was to prevent storing big long-session-only prefixes. But it looks like the TTL was too aggressive for your workload.
[02:08] Mark Ruiz: If TTL was too short, that explains why our long-lived threads aren't benefiting. What would you recommend? Longer TTL or a hybrid LRU-frequency policy?
[02:16] Priya Nair: For Embera specifically, a hybrid works well: keep LRU for ephemeral prefixes but bump TTL for prefixes above a reuse threshold (e.g., seen >5 times in 24h). That reduces churn.
[02:32] Lina Gomez: Is that something we can parameterize? Like a per-tenant threshold?
[02:36] Priya Nair: Yep — Redwood Dedicated/Private configs allow per-tenant prefetch thresholds and TTLs. For the hosted sim we ran per-customer overrides. We'll add a suggested config.
[02:47] Evan Park: Also, on prefetch window — what size did you pick? We saw prefetch size of 6 tokens in the last run.
[02:54] Priya Nair: We tested 6, 12, and 24 token windows. 12 gave the best balance; 24 increased hit-rate slightly but bumped the CPU/kernel cost for some models. So we recommended 12 as default.
[03:10] Mark Ruiz: I remember cost trade-offs were important for us. Did you do any per-token cost delta for those runs?
[03:16] Alex Jensen: Yes, we included a rough unit cost delta in the spreadsheet — 12-token prefetch added ~6% token CPU overhead but yielded ~18% more KV hits in the median run, so net per-response cost tends to decrease because fewer tokens are re-generated. We'll share the trimmed sheet.
[03:36] Lina Gomez: Can you drop that sheet in the Slack channel? The large sheet earlier had a bunch of columns we don't need.
[03:42] Alex Jensen: Absolutely — we'll trim to the key metrics: hit-rate by cohort, latency P50/P95, and delta cost per 1k requests.
[03:50] Priya Nair: One other subtlety — prefix coalescing. We found that sometimes small semantic differences like timezones or IDs prevented reuse. We added a lightweight coalescer that masks obvious entity tokens (IDs, timestamps) before hashing the prefix key. That bumped hit-rate for a subset of queries.
[04:12] Mark Ruiz: That makes sense. We worry about accidentally masking things that change answer content — did you test fidelity?
[04:19] Priya Nair: We ran automated evals on the prompt set (50k prompts) to ensure top-1 generation alignment; fidelity drop was under 0.5% in those cases, mostly in prompts where the entity materially changed the response. We have a safety opt-out to avoid coalescing for intents flagged as sensitive.
[04:38] Evan Park: About session affinity — you suggested we try session pinning to ensure the same backend serves repeated requests, which should help KV locality. What will that change operationally?
[04:47] Alex Jensen: With session affinity we can keep KV entries warmer on the same node and reduce cross-node misses. It does trade off a bit of load balancer flexibility. For the POC we'll enable sticky sessions for the test pool. Should be simple flag in the routing policy.
[05:03] Lina Gomez: Any concerns about availability? If a node goes down, will sessions remap and cold-start?
[05:08] Priya Nair: Yes there will be a fallback to cross-node routing; we also have automatic pre-warm heuristics that will prefetch top prefixes when a session migrates. Not perfect but keeps the hit-rate from collapsing to zero.
[05:22] Mark Ruiz: I want to circle back on measurement — we track both absolute hit-rate and effective token savings. Is Redwood's measurement tool calculating both?
[05:30] Priya Nair: Our analytics reports compute: raw KV hits, token savings (approx), and cost-adjusted savings using CPU token unit cost. We also compute a reconciled metric — percentage of responses where cached prefix avoided generation of N tokens.
[05:46] Alex Jensen: Quick demo — (screen share) here's the shaded region where the last change went live, you can see the prefix hit spike at 02:10 in the run window.
[05:58] [screen share noise, beeps]
[06:04] Evan Park: I see the spike, but there's a dip a few hours later, looks like around your eviction policy kicking in.
[06:09] Priya Nair: Correct — that's TTL. For the 24h run we propose: session-affinity on, prefetch window 12, coalescer enabled for non-sensitive intents, and hybrid TTL-frequency eviction.
[06:21] Mark Ruiz: Sounds good. On the test plan, is there a timeline for the run and what success thresholds we should check?
[06:28] Alex Jensen: We suggested: run 24h with production replay, look for session hit-rate >40% and token savings >12% on median; if both achieved we can move to a 7-day elevated run and start drafting pilot SLA language.
[06:42] Lina Gomez: Those thresholds look reasonable. For the replay, we'll need the routing flag and a small script to feed past traffic, Evan can do that.
[06:50] Evan Park: Yep, I'll enable the flag 2026-08-07 and run the replay overnight into 08-08. I'll notify infra channel when done.
[06:58] Priya Nair: We'll prepare the runbook steps for enabling the flag and the config snippet. Also we'll add a short checklist to compare the before/after graphs and the trimmed benchmark sheet.
[07:10] Mark Ruiz: Any red flags from a compliance standpoint? We noticed some hashed keys contain PHI-esque tokens in a few prompts — are we okay with masking?
[07:19] Alex Jensen: We flagged that in the sample set. The coalescer can be configured to exclude any prefixes where tokens match a PHI regex; in Private deployments you can also disable coalescing entirely. We'll include the policy in the runbook.
[07:34] Lina Gomez: Good. Also, can you add an item to capture examples of false positives where coalescing changed outputs? We want to audit those.
[07:40] Priya Nair: Will do — we'll collect a small sample set and annotate.
[07:44] Alex Jensen: Quick recap of action items — Alex will send trimmed sheet, Priya will send runbook, Evan will flip flag and run replay, Lina will share top prefixes and samples. Any other items?
[07:56] Mark Ruiz: We'll follow up with our legal on the PHI masking but otherwise good.
[08:02] Evan Park: One more note — we saw a slight bump in p95 latency when prefetch window increased to 24. Just flagging for monitoring.
[08:10] Priya Nair: Noted. That's why we prefer 12 by default; we'll monitor P95 and abort if there's >10% degradation.
[08:18] Alex Jensen: Great. We'll target sending the sheet and runbook by Friday 2026-08-06. Next sync? Should we pencil in a 48h post-run review on 2026-08-09?
[08:29] Mark Ruiz: Works for us.
[08:31] Lina Gomez: Yep.
[08:33] Evan Park: Fine for infra.
[08:35] Alex Jensen: Thanks everyone. We'll drop links in Slack.
[08:39] [meeting ends]
